correctness.rationale: Malicki's full open-access text defines \(\mathcal K_N^\prec\), states that the same classes with order-preserving ball-preserving injections are Fraisse classes, and proves that bp-bijections are exactly the bijections preserving strict distance comparisons. Petrov's full arXiv text proves that finite ultrametric spaces are bp-isomorphic exactly when their representing rooted trees are isomorphic. Convex order canonically orders the children at every ball, while the \(r\)-polygon bound is exactly the internal branching bound \(N\); hence finite bp-types are the claimed plane rooted trees. Fraisse extension makes these precisely the finite orbit types. Labeling the ordered tuple coordinates contributes \(n!\); root decomposition gives the stated functional equation; equality patterns give the Stirling transform. Independent recurrence calculations reproduced Catalan \(1,1,2,5,14,42,\ldots\) for \(N=2\) and little Schröder \(1,1,3,11,45,197,\ldots\) for \(N=\infty\).
correctness.risk: The statement concerns the ball-preserving group and its bp-Fraisse category, not the ordinary isometry group where numerical radii remain invariants.

value.rationale: Oligomorphic profiles are natural invariants of permutation groups. The theorem gives an exact profile for a whole family of ordered ultrametric ball-preserving groups, interpolating between two familiar tree sequences and extending from injective to arbitrary tuples. This is a motivated exact invariant rather than an arbitrary finite enumeration.
value.risk: The enumerative step is elementary once the finite bp-types are recognized as plane trees.

final_claim: For the order-preserving ball-preserving group \(G_N=\mathrm{BP}_\prec(\mathbb U_N^\prec)\), injective \(n\)-tuple orbits are counted by \(a_{N,n}=n!t_{N,n}\), where \(t_{N,n}\) counts plane rooted trees with \(n\) leaves and every internal outdegree in \(\{2,\ldots,N\}\). Thus \(T_N(z)=z+\sum_{j=2}^N T_N(z)^j\) (and \(T_\infty=z+T_\infty^2/(1-T_\infty)\)), giving Catalan numbers for \(N=2\), little Schröder numbers for \(N=\infty\), and all-tuple profile \(b_{N,n}=\sum_k S(n,k)a_{N,k}\).
limitations: The formulas do not retain metric-radius data and therefore do not describe ordinary isometry-group profiles.
